## Overview

This project documents my **kit cutting** workflow as a **Composite Technician** at **Eagle Composite**: preparing ply kits from engineering data, operating the **kit cutting machine**, and delivering labeled, traceable cut patterns ready for layup. Accuracy at this stage prevents costly rework in lamination and cure.

## Background of the Study

Composite parts are built from stacked **plies** (oriented carbon fiber or fiberglass layers). Each ply must match the **engineering drawing** and **lamination schedule** (fiber direction, sequence, and material grade). Manual cutting is slow and error-prone; **automated kit cutting** uses a digital nest and cutter to reproduce shapes consistently from roll or sheet stock.

## Motivation of the Study

- **Reduce scrap** through optimized nesting on the cutting table  
- **Improve traceability** (lot number, material spec, ply ID on every kit)  
- **Align production** with drawing revisions before material reaches the clean room  
- **Bridge IT/analytical skills** with physical manufacturing discipline learned on the floor  

## Tools & Equipment

| Item | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| Kit cutting machine | Automated ply cutting from digital nest files |
| Cutting table / vacuum hold-down | Secure material during cut |
| Engineering drawing & lamination schedule | Authority for ply shape, orientation, sequence |
| Material traveler / job traveler | Lot traceability and build history |
| Calipers, scales, labels | Verify kit completeness and mark ply ID |
| PPE (gloves, eye protection) | Safe handling of fibers and tooling |

## Step-by-Step Workflow

### Step 1 — Receive the job package

1. Collect the **work order**, **engineering drawing** (latest revision), and **lamination schedule**.  
2. Confirm **material specification** (e.g., prepreg grade, areal weight, resin system) matches the traveler.  
3. Note **quantity** of kits required and due date for layup.

### Step 2 — Verify drawing and nest data

1. Open the **cut file** or nest layout linked to the drawing revision.  
2. Cross-check **ply names/numbers** against the lamination schedule (0°, 45°, 90°, etc.).  
3. If revision mismatch is found, **stop** and notify engineering or lead before cutting.

### Step 3 — Prepare material

1. Pull roll or sheet stock per traveler **lot number**; record on traveler.  
2. Inspect for **damage, wrinkles, or out-of-life** material (freezer time for prepreg).  
3. Acclimate material per shop procedure if required before cutting.

### Step 4 — Load machine and set parameters

1. Load cut file into **kit cutting machine** software.  
2. Set **knife depth**, **speed**, and **vacuum** per material type and machine checklist.  
3. Position material on table; enable vacuum hold-down; confirm nest fits usable area.

### Step 5 — Execute test cut (when required)

1. Run **test coupon** or first ply outline on scrap when process is new or material lot changed.  
2. Verify **fiber direction arrow** on nest matches drawing convention.  
3. Adjust parameters if fraying, incomplete cut, or offset detected.

### Step 6 — Run production cut

1. Start full nest cut; monitor for **jamming, slip, or vacuum loss**.  
2. Do not leave machine unattended during critical cuts for flight-critical parts.  
3. On alarm, follow **stop-safe** procedure before restarting.

### Step 7 — De-nest, label, and kit

1. Remove cut plies carefully to avoid **fiber distortion**.  
2. Label each ply with **ply ID, orientation, job number, and date**.  
3. Place plies in **kit bag or sequenced stack** per lamination order.  
4. Include **offcuts disposition** note if shop tracks scrap.

### Step 8 — Quality check and release

1. Compare kit against **ply count checklist** on drawing.  
2. Spot-check **critical dimensions** with template or scale for first article.  
3. Sign traveler **cut complete** and deliver to layup or freezer storage.

## Quality Control & Safety

- **FOD control:** Keep table and kits free of debris; no food/drink in cutting area.  
- **Revision control:** Only cut from **released** drawing rev.  
- **Material life:** Track out-time for prepreg; reject expired material.  
- **PPE:** Cut-resistant gloves when handling sharp edges; respiratory policy per facility.  

## Outcomes & Skills Gained

- Reliable **kit cutting machine** operation and nest verification  
- **Material traceability** discipline for aerospace-style production  
- Ability to catch **drawing errors early** before lamination  
- Foundation for **CNC** and **engineering drawing** workflows on the same build
